A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with DEAN renamed SPIN in v2. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original fairness/privacy evaluations, general-capability results, representation analyses and robustness experiments across multiple language models.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds neuron-localization comparisons, safety–privacy experiments, runtime measurements and further capability evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 and Algorithm 1 retain the same gradient-based importance scores, intersection of task-related neuron sets, exclusion of general-capability neurons and zeroing of selected weights. DEAN-to-SPIN renaming and alternative localization experiments do not change the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds a privacy–safety scenario using safety-related BeaverTails data and SALAD-bench's Toxic Content subset. Coverage also expands to AG News, IMDB, SummEval, QAGS, FaithEval's unanswerable/inconsistent settings, TruthfulQA and HaluEval-QA, substantially broadening the evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: The FFT, LoRA, DoRA and ReFT baselines remain. Figure 4 adds Random, Wanda and SparseGPT as alternative neuron-locating methods within the suppression framework across four model families. This introduces substantive direct controls for the localization component beyond the original fine-tuning comparisons.

E3.justification: The added evaluations introduce UniEval relevance scoring, FaithEval accuracy, and hallucination assessment through lm-evaluation-harness and HaluEval. Appendix F adds HSIC evaluations at sigma values 100, 200, 300 and 400. Existing training budgets and extraction settings remain unchanged; the newly specified sigma=50 for Figure 2 is additional disclosure.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of the neuron-localization choice, HSIC kernel-width sensitivity, and paired model-response case studies in Appendix I. These extend scrutiny of the mechanism and its outputs. The earlier malicious-data, dataset-size, extraction-ratio/module and word-frequency analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without experimental run/seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. The additional results retain this reporting practice.

E6.justification: New results cover localization controls, runtime, safety–privacy behavior, additional capabilities and HSIC sensitivity. For example, v2 Table 7 reports Qwen2 privacy/safety scores of 0.8158/0.7190 versus the original model's 0.7412/0.6720 in the new setting. Matched original fairness/privacy, model-size, general-capability and privacy-only fine-tuning table values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 replaces the shared-Z non-strict inequality with distinct Z1/Z2 variables and a strict inequality assuming I[Z1;Z2|X,Y]>0; Appendix B supplies a revised proof. Proposition 1 replaces averaged representations with layer-specific original/modified-model representations and asserts strict reduction under an explicit coupling assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add the claim that SPIN can generalize beyond fairness–privacy trade-offs, supported by the safety extension. The central claims about simultaneous awareness improvements, general-capability preservation and robustness to limited or malicious data remain, including the same headline improvement percentages.

C2.justification: Section 2, Appendix H and the new Limitations section substantially clarify scope. They distinguish appropriate responses from sensitivity and deeper understanding, distinguish privacy awareness from training-time privacy preservation, discuss localization and capability-preservation mechanisms, and acknowledge unresolved intervention during training and coarse module-level analysis.

D1.justification: Appendix F newly documents filtering keywords, safe-answer selection, three-annotator intersection and sampling for the existing datasets, plus Figure 2's sigma value. v2 also supplies evaluation frameworks, localization formulas and runtime information, and changes the code pointer to SPIN. These disclosures do not establish changed original experiments; v1's blanket default evaluation-harness statement is omitted.

R1.justification: The core PEFT and neuron-localization positioning remains. Added citations cover pruning, privacy-preserving training, over-refusal and the new evaluations. Appendices A/H refine the distinction from traditional fairness/differential-privacy research and explicitly claim that prior work had not explored the LLM awareness trade-off.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper and renames the method, replaces the main related-work section with a problem statement, and relocates related work, the algorithm and model-size discussion to appendices. A contents page and reorganized experimental and discussion sections substantially change the document's structure.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a predominantly two-column document. v2 expands the general-capability table, adds localization and HSIC-sensitivity figures, introduces several experimental tables and boxed QA examples, and relocates existing displays such as the model-size table and word-frequency figure.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validation gaps through direct localization controls, HSIC sensitivity tests and broader checks of generation quality (Figures 4/8 and Table 8). The revised conditional argument, fuller data-curation documentation and explicit scope limitations also improve assessability. Mixed new capability scores and absent uncertainty reporting still limit blanket preservation claims, but the stronger controls and transparency substantially improve the paper's evidential support.
